record.paper_title: Open Problems and Conjectures Related to the Theory of Mathematical Quasicrystals
record.original_question: Does every one-dimensional self-similar inflation tiling with Pisot scaling factor λ have pure point spectrum whenever its abelianisation (substitution) matrix M has irreducible characteristic polynomial, equivalently whenever the algebraic degree of λ equals the dimension of M?

evidence.quote: Conjecture 2.2.1 (Pisot substitution conjecture) A one-dimensional self-similar inflation tiling with Pisot scaling factor λ has pure point spectrum if its abelianisation matrix (i.e. its substitution matrix) M has an irreducible characteristic polynomial; that is, if the algebraic degree of λ equals the dimension of M (or the number of tile types).

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Setup. Let A = {1, 2, ..., n} be a finite alphabet with associated prototiles (closed intervals) of positive lengths ℓ_1, ..., ℓ_n. A one-dimensional self-similar inflation rule with scaling factor λ > 1 is a map that sends each prototile of length ℓ_i to a finite concatenation of prototiles whose total length is λℓ_i. Its abelianisation (substitution) matrix M ∈ ℤ_{≥0}^{n×n} has entries M_{ij} equal to the number of tiles of type i appearing in the inflation of the prototile of type j; the vector (ℓ_1, ..., ℓ_n) is a positive eigenvector of M with eigenvalue λ. Assume M is primitive (so λ is the simple Perron–Frobenius eigenvalue). The associated tiling dynamical system is the orbit closure under translation of any fixed point of the inflation, equipped with the unique invariant probability measure; one says the tiling has pure point (pure discrete) dynamical spectrum if the Koopman representation of the translation action on L^2 of this measure decomposes as a direct sum of one-dimensional eigenspaces.

Assume further that λ is a Pisot number (a real algebraic integer > 1 all of whose Galois conjugates lie strictly inside the open unit disk) and that the characteristic polynomial of M is irreducible over ℚ — equivalently, the algebraic degree of λ over ℚ equals n.

Question. Under the above hypotheses, does the tiling dynamical system necessarily have pure point spectrum?
artifact.status_search_result: The irreducible Pisot substitution conjecture remains open in general. Special cases are known: it holds for two-letter (binary) Pisot substitutions and for β-substitutions when β is a Pisot number. Algorithms exist to verify pure discrete spectrum for individual substitutions, and various reformulations have been given, but no general proof or counterexample is known.

status_evidence.title: Yet another characterization of the Pisot substitution conjecture
status_evidence.snippet: Reformulation of the Pisot substitution conjecture, treating it as still open.
status_evidence.claim: The irreducible Pisot substitution conjecture is treated as a still-open problem.

status_evidence.title: On the Pisot Substitution Conjecture
status_evidence.snippet: Survey discussing partial results and the open status of the conjecture.
status_evidence.claim: The conjecture remains open in the irreducible case; partial results exist.

status_evidence.title: The Pisot Conjecture for β-substitutions
status_evidence.snippet: Proves pure discrete spectrum for β-substitutions when β is a Pisot number.
status_evidence.claim: A special case (β-substitutions with β Pisot) has been resolved.
